scan-framing.title: Morning X-first scan: verification framing per story

meta.method: Each claim is tested by a deterministic Python check against snapshotted source texts and X posts. PASS = the source sentence quoted supports the claim; FAIL = the source contradicts it or a required caveat is missing; NEEDS-HUMAN = opinion or not decidable by string/number match.

results.artifact_sentence: The twist: text-only peer review couldn't tell an honest caveat from a hidden flaw.

results.quote: Only running scripts on the uploaded data overturned nearly half of major objections
results.source_quote: For major objections, the scripts overturned the headline conclusion in 77 of 156 cases (49.4%); for minor objections, in 24 of 120 cases (20.0%). [p20] These are executed referee objections in this journal, not a random audit of all papers in the cohort.
results.note: inverted: the scripts overturned the papers' headline conclusions in 49.4% of major-objection cases, not the objections themselves
results.artifact_sentence: Only running scripts on the uploaded data overturned nearly half of major objections.

results.quote: Airbnb fine-tuned a tiny 2-billion-parameter Gemma model
results.source_quote: We compare a fine-tuned classifier with 2 billion effective parameters (E2B) against open-weight and proprietary models on a held-out evaluation dataset of 10,000 weighted examples. … Fine-tuning Gemma4-E2B on hundreds of thousands of domain-specific examples lifts its F1 from 0.563 to 0.902, on par with the best proprietary models, while median latency stays at 35ms.
results.artifact_sentence: Next, Airbnb fine-tuned a tiny 2-billion-parameter Gemma model that matched frontier APIs in 35 milliseconds at one percent of the cost.
results.check_code:
def check(ctx):
    return ctx.require('airbnb', r'fine-tuned classifier with 2 billion effective parameters', r'Fine-tuning Gemma4-E2B')
